prompt: From a point on level ground $40$ feet from the base of a tree, the angle of elevation to the top of the tree is $\theta$, where $\tan\theta = 1.5$. What is the height of the tree, in feet?
hint: Tangent relates the opposite side (the height) to the adjacent side (the ground distance).

hints.text: Tangent relates the opposite side (the height) to the adjacent side (the ground distance).

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try easy numbers: if $\tan\theta = 2$ and the ground distance is $10$ feet, the height is $2 \times 10 = 20$ feet. Tangent times the adjacent side gives the opposite side.

learningObjective: Use tangent to solve an angle-of-elevation problem.
explanation: The tree, the ground, and the line of sight form a right triangle. The height is opposite the angle; the $40$ feet is adjacent.

alternativeExplanations.title: Tangent is the elevation ratio
steps: Angle-of-elevation and angle-of-depression problems almost always use tangent, because the two known quantities are height and horizontal distance — the two legs.
Sine and cosine appear only when the hypotenuse (the direct line of sight) is involved.
Identifying which two sides the problem hands you selects the ratio immediately.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: Dividing 40 by 1.5 ≈ 26.7 treats tangent as adjacent-over-opposite — the ratio upside down.
Tangent is opposite over adjacent, and the height is the OPPOSITE side here: h = 40 × 1.5. Label the triangle before computing.
